newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM says no force if Lima hostages unharmed.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says no force if Lima hostages unharmed.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Monday that Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori promised him at a weekend summit force would not be used in the Lima hostage crisis unless captives were harmed.
"It (the summit) was successful because I had him (Fujimori) declare in my presence he will not resort to force unless the hostages are injured," Hashimoto told reporters.
Leftist rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) took over the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on December 17 and have demanded the release of about 400 jailed comrades.
They have released most of the hundreds of hostages they took in the attack but still hold 72 key captives, including Japanese ambassador Morihisa Aoki.

Hashimoto, who met Fujimori on Saturday in Toronto, said another key result of the summit was Fujimori's approval for a Japanese representative to join an international peace commission set up to negotiate the release of the hostages.
Hashimoto said the addition of Terusuke Terada, who has been Japan's on-the-spot point man in the crisis, to the commission means "we can get information directly from it."
Terada joins Red Cross mediator Michel Minnig, Canadian ambassador Anthony Vincent and Lima's Roman Catholic Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani.
